sources.title: NavigationView - Windows apps
claims: NavigationView remains the native top-level navigation container and includes keyboard and High Contrast guidance.

sources.title: Open files and folders with Windows App SDK pickers
claims: Windows App SDK 1.8 native pickers accept a WindowId and return selected paths.

sources.title: Progress controls - Windows apps
claims: Use ProgressBar for nonmodal work and ProgressRing only for genuine waits, with explanatory text when needed.

sources.title: Accessibility overview - Windows apps
claims: WinUI accessibility depends on UI Automation, keyboard, semantic XAML order, scalable text, and High Contrast theme resources.

sources.title: UISettings AnimationsEnabled
claims: UISettings.AnimationsEnabled exposes whether custom Windows UI animations are enabled.

sources.title: GitHub Desktop contextual onboarding and next steps
claims: A shipped desktop application gives contextual next steps in first-run and empty states.

sources.title: balenaEtcher guarded source-target-write utility
claims: A shipped desktop write utility prioritizes explicit source, target, safety, verification, and recovery.

candidates.title: Selected Guided Fluent workspace
candidates.user_problem: A first-time or returning player needs one obvious safe next action without optional files, technical report data, or unrelated destinations becoming global blockers.
candidates.reusable_principle: Map the shared conversion kernel into one native application navigator and one scoped task stage whose primary action, reason, progress, and recovery stay together.
candidates.source_expression: Windows supplies an adaptive native navigator and familiar pickers, while shipped desktop onboarding demonstrates contextual next-step guidance for otherwise ambiguous empty states.
candidates.product_expression: Use NavigationView for Convert, History, Advanced, and Settings, then keep Input, Optional or Skip, Dry Run, guarded Write, Result, and Rollback as one ordered workspace with a stable local command footer.

target_adaptations.native_components: NavigationView, Windows App SDK 1.8 FileOpenPicker and FolderPicker, Button, ToggleSwitch, InfoBar, ProgressBar, ContentDialog, Expander, and native text controls.
target_adaptations.navigation: Use exactly one top-level NavigationView; the bounded conversion progress cue communicates state but is not a second navigator.
target_adaptations.density: Maintain Windows desktop density, reflow to one column before clipping, and keep optional and technical detail collapsed until relevant.
target_adaptations.icons: Use licensed WinUI SymbolIcon or existing project vectors paired with localized labels for primary, risky, and recovery commands.
target_adaptations.motion: Use native control feedback plus a short local opacity or visual-state transition for optional reveal and footer state changes only.
target_adaptations.input_behavior: Follow semantic XAML order for Tab, preserve visible focus and focus return after pickers/dialogs, activate with Enter or Space, and cancel confirmation with Escape.

accessibility.reduced_motion: When UISettings.AnimationsEnabled is false, replace custom transition with an immediate state swap and preserve all textual and semantic feedback.
accessibility.non_motion_equivalence: Blocked, ready, running, success, and failure always expose durable text, icon, enabled state, and recovery independent of animation.
accessibility.contrast: Resolve surfaces, foregrounds, borders, and focus visuals through theme resources with HighContrast overrides rather than fixed light colors.
accessibility.non_color: Pair semantic color with a localized status phrase, icon, control state, and labeled Fix action.
accessibility.text_scaling: Wrap labels and reason text, auto-size commands, stack responsive rows, and retain full selected paths in accessible values when visual ellipsis is necessary.
accessibility.focus_input: Keep one deterministic task order and move focus only after explicit route or dialog transitions, never on background status refresh.
accessibility.assistive_tech: Give route title, path picker, primary action, blocked reason, Fix, status, manifest, and rollback stable AutomationIds and use only a scoped polite live region.

motion.trigger: Optional data is enabled or skipped, or a command changes from blocked to ready, running, or result.
motion.timing_intent: Update semantics immediately and use only a short native local transition; never move the primary command frame.
motion.reduced_motion_variant: Instant content/state replacement with persistent text, icon, focus, and automation semantics.
motion.performance_risk: Do not animate ScrollViewer geometry, full pages, blur, shadows, path text, or navigation; prefer compositor-safe opacity where useful.

contraindications: Do not expose optional System, ExtData, or CEC fields until enabled.
Do not duplicate top-level navigation with a persistent stage rail.
Do not place hashes, manifest JSON, or report payloads in the primary hierarchy.

candidates.title: Non-selected compact operation canvas
candidates.user_problem: An expert may want source, current reference, output, authorization, and recovery visible together for repeated repair work.
candidates.reusable_principle: Keep operation identity and its guarded command stable while disclosing technical detail at the exact affected row.
candidates.source_expression: A shipped guarded writer foregrounds explicit source and target identity, while Windows distinguishes nonmodal progress from a wait that truly blocks interaction.
candidates.product_expression: A dense review canvas could align source, current reference, and output above a fixed write control while keeping inspection and rollback details expandable beside their owning operation.

target_adaptations.native_components: Use native picker-backed path rows, scoped InfoBar, ProgressBar for nonmodal work, ProgressRing only for a genuine local wait, ContentDialog for write, and Expander for technical evidence.
target_adaptations.navigation: Retain the same single NavigationView but present Convert as an expert review canvas rather than sequential staged content.
target_adaptations.density: Use compact aligned path rows at wide windows and stack the same rows at the minimum width without shrinking controls.
target_adaptations.icons: Use WinUI symbols with labels for inspect, write, warning, success, and undo; no external product assets.
target_adaptations.motion: Keep the command footer fixed and optionally crossfade only scoped status content; native progress owns running feedback.
target_adaptations.input_behavior: Tab through source, current, output, and the active command before technical disclosures; restore focus after picker and confirmation.

accessibility.reduced_motion: Disable custom crossfade when Windows animations are off and keep only essential native running semantics.
accessibility.non_motion_equivalence: Every operation state has explicit text, icon, enabled state, and actionable recovery.
accessibility.contrast: Use theme and HighContrast resources on every row, divider, status, and focus visual.
accessibility.non_color: Show the sole disabled reason and a labeled Fix command beside the primary action.
accessibility.text_scaling: Reflow the review grid to one column and keep full values available to UI Automation.
accessibility.focus_input: Preserve a deterministic source-current-output-command focus order and return focus to the invoker after dialog cancellation.
accessibility.assistive_tech: Expose selected path values, progress state, confirmation risk, manifest output, and rollback availability through native automation patterns.

motion.trigger: Inspect, Dry Run, Write, or picker selection changes the scoped operation state.
motion.timing_intent: Acknowledge input immediately while the stable command and nearby text explain progress and resolution.
motion.stop_condition: Stop the native progress state when the associated command succeeds, fails, or cancels.
motion.reduced_motion_variant: Immediate status replacement with text and icon; no custom spatial transition.
motion.performance_risk: Avoid custom progress animation and all layout-property animation.

contraindications: Do not copy balenaEtcher branding, copy, exact composition, or assets.
Do not make the expert canvas the default while first-run comprehension is the frozen priority.
Do not leak active conversion blockers into History or Settings.

rejections.idea: Replace the frozen Guided Fluent workspace with the compact expert operation canvas as the default Convert experience.
rejections.reason: It remains technically viable but increases first-run simultaneous choices and weakens the frozen one-stage, one-primary-action contract; retain only its concise review-row ideas inside progressive disclosure.

rejections.idea: Restore a decorative hero, repeated stage rail, global readiness badge, repeated next-step banners, and always-visible optional paths.
rejections.reason: The structure duplicates hierarchy and makes optional or technical state appear globally blocking instead of keeping one scoped task action and recovery.

rejections.idea: Add full-page slides, staggered forms, hover lift, looping empty-state art, failure shake, or success confetti.
rejections.reason: These patterns do not explain conversion state and add focus, motion-preference, and performance costs to an operational safety tool.

contradictions.conflict: Top-level NavigationView and contextual sequential guidance can become duplicate navigation if both are interactive route systems.
contradictions.resolution: NavigationView owns application destinations only; the conversion sequence is a non-navigational status/progress cue plus one local primary action.

contradictions.conflict: A risky write benefits from guarded, potentially blocking feedback, while Inspect and Dry Run should not freeze unrelated navigation.
contradictions.resolution: Scope progress and disabled controls to the active command, reserve ContentDialog and blocking wait behavior for the write boundary, and leave unrelated destinations usable.

limitations: The shipped-product lane is public release and repository evidence, not a newly captured interactive Windows session or paid flow database.
GitHub Desktop onboarding evidence is historical and only supports contextual next-step behavior, not current Windows visual styling.
The balenaEtcher artifact supports the guarded source-target-write principle but does not contain a complete adjacent-state screenshot set.
This research revalidation does not prove runtime WinUI layout, keyboard focus, UI Automation, High Contrast, text scaling, or motion; those require capture and isolated verification on Windows.
